Splatting is a form of volume compositing (specifically, additive blending of projected primitives, which is mathematically equivalent to front-to-back blending in the limit of small splats or can be viewed as a specific integration method). The evidence explicitly mentions that the base algorithm projects voxels and distributes energy to pixels (compositing into the framebuffer/screen plane). While the paper focuses on *optimization* (culling), it relies on the standard splatting/compositing mechanism for the final image formation. The claim describes the fundamental operation of the method discussed (compositing via splatting/integration). Therefore, the evidence supports the claim that the method involves compositing into the framebuffer using standard volume compositing techniques (splatting/integration).

A voxel is fully occluded if, for all pixels $(x, y)$ in its footprint, the current Buffer Plane value $B[x, y]$ is less than $Z_v$ (meaning a closer voxel already covers that area) [S1, unofficial].

The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly describes the optimization steps for occlusion culling. Specifically, 'Optimization Step 2' states that the algorithm iterates through the model and projects voxels onto a buffer plane, filling pixels with the voxel's Z-value if it is less than the current pixel value (depth comparison). 'Optimization Step 3' states that only voxels whose projection exists at least partially (i.e., they were not fully occluded) are selected for rendering. The 'Occlusion Culling Logic' note further clarifies that a voxel is discarded if its projected radius is completely covered by radii of points closer to the screen (smaller Z). This aligns perfectly with the claim that a voxel is fully occluded if, for all pixels in its footprint, the buffer value is less than the voxel's Z-value.
